name: Westbridge High School
description: A bright, contemporary North American high school of roughly 1,000 students, with broad windows, an open atrium, locker-lined corridors, a library, arts and athletic facilities, and a sheltered courtyard. Home of the Westbridge Hawks, whose navy-and-silver colours appear throughout the campus. A flexible everyday setting with no predefined students, staff or plot.

nodes.name: Westbridge High School
nodes.description: A coeducational four-grade high school serving roughly 1,000 students. Its two-storey academic wing, shared activity spaces and gym frame a sheltered courtyard. The school is known as the Westbridge Hawks; navy blue and silver appear on its signs, sports uniforms and awards, without dominating every room.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale buff brick, generous full-height glazing, warm timber soffits and navy directional signs create a modern, well-maintained campus. A narrow blue tile line leads across the bright atrium toward the courtyard; a restrained silver hawk crest appears beside the entrance. A rain garden softens the front approach.

detail.place.purpose: Secondary education, independent study, clubs, athletics, performances, student services and community events.
detail.place.layout: From the south, a student-and-staff parking lot connects by walkway to the front plaza and glazed atrium. Academic corridors extend east, with a stair to a second floor of additional classrooms; the library and administrative suite are west-front. The auditorium, music room and cafeteria open from rear passages. North-facing atrium doors lead to a courtyard, whose enclosed north connector reaches the gym; a controlled path continues to the outdoor field. Only representative rooms are mapped.
detail.place.access: The main vestibule is monitored during the school day; visitors report to reception. Students use scheduled entrances and school facilities according to their timetables. Kitchen deliveries, athletic grounds and after-hours events have separate controlled access; fire exits remain available for emergency egress.
detail.place.routines: Before school the parking lot and plaza fill, lockers open and morning notices appear. Short, crowded class changes punctuate teaching periods; students spread between cafeteria, courtyard and library at lunch. Clubs, band rehearsals and Hawks practices continue after the final bell.
detail.place.resources: Teaching rooms, lockers, library, student services, cafeteria, auditorium, music and art rooms, science lab, gym, changing rooms, field, accessible lift and the posted school calendar.
detail.place.obstacles: Bell-time crowding affects corridors, stairs and doorways. Facilities may be reserved, supervised or locked outside scheduled use; ordinary classrooms and service spaces beyond the named examples exist without individual map nodes.

detail.design.form: Contemporary two-storey school campus with glazed atrium and open courtyard.
detail.design.materials: Pale buff brick, full-height glazing and timber soffits
detail.design.distinctive: Thin blue atrium tile line, silver hawk crest and front rain garden

nodes.name: Student and staff parking lot
nodes.description: An ordinary paved parking area for student drivers, staff vehicles and after-school event parking, separated from the bus curb and main pedestrian plaza.
nodes.visualDescription: Marked asphalt bays, a few small planted islands, bicycle warning signs and navy-and-silver WESTBRIDGE HAWKS directional markers flank a sidewalk leading toward the glass entrance.

detail.place.purpose: Parking, arrivals, departures and meeting rides.
detail.place.layout: Southwest of the front plaza, a marked pedestrian walkway leads from the parking bays to the plaza. A vehicle driveway meets the public street; the bus drop-off curb is on the separate plaza side. The school entrance is visible beyond the front plaza, but pedestrians must follow the marked walkway rather than crossing the bus curb.
detail.place.access: Student and staff bays are signed; visitors use designated spaces and check in at the main entrance. The lot does not connect to the kitchen service lane.
detail.place.routines: Mostly fills before first bell, thins during the afternoon and becomes busy at dismissal or evening games.
detail.place.resources: Marked parking spaces, lighting, accessible bays, pedestrian walkway, bike-warning signs and waste bins.
detail.place.obstacles: Slow-moving vehicles, poor visibility between parked cars and winter snowbanks complicate walking routes.

detail.design.form: Marked asphalt bays, a few small planted islands, bicycle warning signs and navy-and-silver WESTBRIDGE HAWKS directional markers flank a sidewalk leading toward the glass entrance.
detail.design.materials: Asphalt bays, planted islands and pedestrian sidewalk
detail.design.distinctive: Westbridge Hawks signs beside the parking walkway

nodes.name: Front plaza
nodes.description: A broad pedestrian approach to the school entrance, busy with arriving students, bikes and people meeting before and after classes.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale concrete pavers, low timber benches, bicycle hoops and a planted rain garden sit below the glass atrium. Navy lettering spells WESTBRIDGE HIGH SCHOOL beneath a small silver hawk emblem.

detail.place.purpose: Arrivals, departures, informal meetings and waiting for pickup.
detail.place.layout: The main doors face south across the plaza. A pedestrian walkway runs southwest to the adjacent student-and-staff parking lot, and another path meets the public sidewalk and bus drop-off curb. The plaza doors lead directly into the entrance atrium; delivery vehicles have no route through it.
detail.place.access: The main vestibule is supervised during school hours. Public paths remain usable for arrivals; exterior doors are secured outside scheduled access periods.
detail.place.routines: Students gather here before the first bell, then disperse into classes. At dismissal, bikes roll out, school buses load at the curb and students wait for rides or walk to the parking lot.
detail.place.resources: Bike hoops, benches, exterior school sign, covered doorway, accessible ramp and sheltered waiting spot.
detail.place.obstacles: People on foot and bicycles converge at the entrance; snow, ice or wet paving can make the approach slippery.

detail.design.form: Pale concrete pavers, low timber benches, bicycle hoops and a planted rain garden sit below the glass atrium.
detail.design.materials: Concrete pavers and timber benches
detail.design.distinctive: Bicycle hoops, rain garden and school name under hawk emblem

nodes.name: Entrance atrium
nodes.description: The two-storey entrance atrium and main social crossroads, connecting classrooms, administration, the library, performance and dining areas, and the courtyard.
nodes.visualDescription: Daylight falls onto pale terrazzo through two-storey glass. A thin blue floor line points toward the courtyard; suspended translucent panels float above the staircase. A glass-fronted trophy display holds Hawks awards, with a silver hawk crest on the wall beside rotating club and game posters.

detail.place.purpose: Main circulation, visitor reception, announcements and casual student gathering.
detail.place.layout: The secure vestibule and front plaza are south. Reception and the administrative passage are to the right, the library is left, and the classroom corridor opens to the east beside the main stair and lift. A rear-left passage serves the auditorium and music room; a rear-right passage reaches the cafeteria. Glazed north doors open to the courtyard. The courtyard benches and three silver birches are visible through the north glazing; the doors, not the windows, provide the outside route.
detail.place.access: Visitors check in at reception. Teaching-wing doors and courtyard doors follow the school schedule; the public can remain in the reception portion without entering teaching spaces.
detail.place.routines: Students converge to meet friends and check notices before the bell. Clubs advertise activities on the board; Hawks scores and school announcements rotate on the screen. Traffic ebbs during lessons.
detail.place.resources: Reception counter, accessible lift, trophy display, public noticeboard, digital announcement screen, benches, drinking fountain and directional signs. A thin blue tile line across the atrium, silver Hawks emblem, and navy-and-silver event displays identify the school.
detail.place.obstacles: The stairs, classroom doors and reception area pinch at class changes; conversations echo across the high glass-lined space.

detail.design.form: Daylight falls onto pale terrazzo through two-storey glass.
detail.design.materials: Terrazzo floor, two-storey glazing and clear display cases
detail.design.colours: Pale terrazzo, navy blue and silver
detail.design.distinctive: Blue floor line, hanging translucent panels, trophy case and crest

nodes.name: Main stair and upper landing
nodes.description: The broad stair and mezzanine that link the atrium to the second-floor teaching corridors. The upper level contains ordinary rooms that are not mapped individually.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale oak handrails and grey treads with navy-blue edge strips rise behind a clear balustrade. The atrium’s hanging translucent panels are visible from the landing.

detail.place.purpose: Movement between floors and short pauses between classes.
detail.place.layout: A broad stair rises from the east side of the atrium beside the classroom-corridor entrance to a mezzanine and unmapped upstairs teaching corridors. A lift beside the lower stair provides step-free access.
detail.place.access: Students use the stair during normal circulation. The landing is not a designated waiting area during busy changes, and the lift remains available for access needs.
detail.place.routines: Class-change traffic moves both ways; the upper window seats are sometimes used for reading or quiet conversations at break.
detail.place.resources: Handrails, lift access, wall clock, directional signs and a few recessed window seats.
detail.place.obstacles: During class changes the stair is crowded, and voices on the upper landing can be heard from the atrium below.

detail.design.form: Pale oak handrails and grey treads with navy-blue edge strips rise behind a clear balustrade.
detail.design.materials: Pale oak handrails, grey stair treads and clear balustrade
detail.design.distinctive: Hanging atrium panels remain visible from the landing

nodes.name: Academic wing and classroom corridor
nodes.description: The ground-floor academic wing, with its main locker-lined corridor and adjacent teaching rooms, separate student washrooms, art studio and science laboratory, connects the atrium to the courtyard.
nodes.visualDescription: Tall windows illuminate pale-grey lockers with navy number plates. Classroom doors have glazed sidelights; club flyers, exam notices and student art cluster around the drinking fountain, while the floors remain visibly clean and regularly maintained.

detail.place.purpose: Connecting teaching rooms and providing student storage.
detail.place.layout: Enter through the east atrium doors. Near the entrance are the general classroom and two separately signed student washrooms. The art studio is midway along the courtyard-facing side, and the science lab is near the north end. A glazed door at the end opens to the courtyard. Additional classrooms branch off this corridor but are not mapped.
detail.place.access: Students use their assigned lockers and timetabled rooms. Both washrooms are entered from the main corridor, not through one another. The courtyard door is supervised and secured outside normal movement times.
detail.place.routines: Students stop at lockers between classes, queue outside teaching rooms and read club notices; the corridor is relatively quiet during lessons.
detail.place.resources: Student lockers, corridor notice strips, water fountain, recycling bins, charging shelf and wayfinding signs.
detail.place.obstacles: Open locker doors and groups waiting outside rooms reduce walking space during bells; conversations are easily overheard.

detail.design.form: Tall windows illuminate pale-grey lockers with navy number plates.
detail.design.materials: Metal locker banks, windows and glazed door sidelights
detail.design.colours: Pale grey with navy number plates
detail.design.distinctive: Student artwork, club flyers and exam notices along the corridor

nodes.name: General classroom
nodes.description: A representative high-school classroom used for literature, mathematics, social studies, exam preparation and clubs; the building has many more ordinary classrooms that are not individually mapped.
nodes.visualDescription: Large windows face the courtyard above rearrangeable pale-wood desks. A broad whiteboard, interactive display and navy-edged bulletin board give the room a practical, familiar appearance.

detail.place.purpose: Routine lessons, group work, tutoring and after-school clubs.
detail.place.layout: The entrance opens near the beginning of the classroom corridor. Desk groups face the teaching wall, and a lockable supply cupboard sits along the corridor-side wall. Tall windows overlook the courtyard planting beds and paths; there is no direct classroom exit outdoors.
detail.place.access: Students enter for scheduled classes or with staff permission. The cabinet and teaching equipment are managed by staff.
detail.place.routines: Different classes use the room across the day. Desks shift between lectures, group projects and tests, and student work remains displayed until the next project cycle.
detail.place.resources: Rearrangeable desks, whiteboard, interactive display, school supplies, reference materials and a shared projector.
detail.place.obstacles: Furniture and bags can block sightlines when groups form; noise from passing classes filters through the corridor door.

detail.design.form: Large windows face the courtyard above rearrangeable pale-wood desks.
detail.design.materials: Pale-wood movable desks and broad glazed windows
detail.design.distinctive: Interactive display and navy-edged bulletin board

nodes.name: Boys' washroom
nodes.description: A standard student washroom near the beginning of the academic corridor, with a short privacy entry, toilet stalls and sinks.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale tiled walls, charcoal stall partitions, long mirrors, stainless fixtures and a small navy wall sign. Frosted high windows admit daylight.

detail.place.purpose: Student toilet and handwashing facilities.
detail.place.layout: One signed entrance opens directly off the classroom corridor near the general classroom. A short angled entry screens the sinks and stalls from the hall; no internal connection leads to the girls’ washroom.
detail.place.access: For normal student use during building hours, with routine cleaning and temporary closures as necessary. Accessible single-user facilities elsewhere in the school need not be mapped separately.
detail.place.routines: Quiet during most lessons, busier at breaks and lunch; custodial checks occur on a regular schedule.
detail.place.resources: Toilet stalls, sinks, mirrors, soap and paper dispensers, hand dryers and waste bins.
detail.place.obstacles: The narrow entry can become crowded between bells; tiled surfaces make noise carry.

detail.design.form: Pale tiled walls, charcoal stall partitions, long mirrors, stainless fixtures and a small navy wall sign.
detail.design.materials: Tiled walls, metal fixtures and stall partitions
detail.design.distinctive: High frosted windows and long mirrors

nodes.name: Girls' washroom
nodes.description: A separate, conventional student washroom near the beginning of the academic corridor, with toilets, sinks and mirrors.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale tile, charcoal stall doors, a long wall mirror, stainless sinks and a navy room sign match the school’s clean contemporary finishes.

detail.place.purpose: Student toilet and handwashing facilities.
detail.place.layout: A separate signed door opens off the classroom corridor opposite and slightly farther north than the boys’ washroom. An angled entry leads to sinks and private stalls; there is no door joining the two washrooms.
detail.place.access: For normal student use during building hours, subject to custodial servicing or temporary closure. Additional accessible single-user facilities exist elsewhere without separate map nodes.
detail.place.routines: Students visit at breaks, lunch and between lessons, while routine custodial checks are scheduled during quieter periods.
detail.place.resources: Toilet stalls, sinks, mirrors, soap and paper dispensers, hand dryers and waste bins.
detail.place.obstacles: Queues can extend toward the corridor at busy times; the room has limited conversational privacy.

detail.design.form: Pale tile, charcoal stall doors, a long wall mirror, stainless sinks and a navy room sign match the school’s clean contemporary finishes.
detail.design.materials: Tile, metal sinks and stall partitions
detail.design.distinctive: Long wall mirror and signed entrance

nodes.name: Science laboratory
nodes.description: A supervised practical room for demonstrations and student experiments, with a small preparation alcove reserved for staff.
nodes.visualDescription: White worktops with charcoal sink basins, slate-blue stools, glass-fronted equipment cupboards and high windows make the laboratory bright and uncluttered. A blue safety placard hangs by the door.

detail.place.purpose: Science instruction, demonstrations and supervised practical experiments.
detail.place.layout: A single student entrance opens near the far end of the classroom corridor. Island benches occupy the centre; sinks and a demonstration station run along the outer wall. A lockable preparation alcove is behind the teaching station.
detail.place.access: Practical activities require staff supervision. Chemical storage and the preparation alcove are staff-only.
detail.place.routines: Lessons alternate between desk work and practical setups; equipment is checked and returned after each session.
detail.place.resources: Microscopes, measuring equipment, sinks, washable safety goggles, eye-wash station, demonstration display and locked chemical storage.
detail.place.obstacles: Benches limit free movement, and active experiments require clear aisles and safety procedures.

detail.design.form: White worktops with charcoal sink basins, slate-blue stools, glass-fronted equipment cupboards and high windows make the laboratory bright and uncluttered.
detail.design.materials: White worktops, sink basins and glass-fronted cupboards
detail.design.distinctive: Blue safety placard beside the laboratory door

nodes.name: Art studio
nodes.description: A flexible arts classroom where students can paint, build models, make posters and prepare displays for the rest of the school.
nodes.visualDescription: North-facing windows light long worktables, drying racks and shelves of sketchbooks. Brushes hang from pegboards beside a student-made mosaic in blues and earth tones.

detail.place.purpose: Visual arts lessons, making projects, and preparing school displays.
detail.place.layout: The art studio opens from the middle of the classroom corridor; tables occupy the centre, with sinks and drying racks at the far wall and secure tool storage by the teaching station.
detail.place.access: Open for scheduled lessons and supervised clubs. Some tools and supplies remain in staff-controlled storage.
detail.place.routines: Works in progress stay on labelled racks; student displays rotate through the atrium and hallway.
detail.place.resources: Worktables, easels, sinks, paper cutters, drying racks, basic art supplies and lockable cupboards.
detail.place.obstacles: Wet work needs drying space and clear tabletops; the room can smell faintly of paint even after cleanup.

detail.design.form: North-facing windows light long worktables, drying racks and shelves of sketchbooks.
detail.design.materials: Long worktables, pegboards and drying racks
detail.design.colours: Blues and earth tones in the student mosaic
detail.design.distinctive: North-facing windows and student-made mosaic

nodes.name: Library and media centre
nodes.description: A daylight-filled library and media centre with books, study booths, a browsing area for student publications and room for both quiet work and small group projects.
nodes.visualDescription: Low pale-oak shelves preserve sightlines to the courtyard windows. Blue upholstered reading seats surround a curved borrowing desk, and glass-fronted study booths line the quieter wall. A small display shelf holds school yearbooks and copies of the student newspaper.

detail.place.purpose: Reading, research, individual study and supervised group work.
detail.place.layout: Enter from the west side of the atrium opposite reception. The circulation desk faces the entrance; lending shelves fill the centre, while study booths and computer desks sit by the north windows. A student-publications shelf is near the desk. North-facing windows overlook the courtyard, but the library entrance remains on the atrium side.
detail.place.access: Open during posted library hours. Quiet booths can be reserved and classes use the space with staff supervision.
detail.place.routines: Early arrivals take the window seats before classes; lunch brings readers and students finishing assignments. After school, project groups, tutors and students preparing for exams use the study booths.
detail.place.resources: Lending collection, yearbook and school newspaper shelf, catalogue computers, printers, research terminals, study booths and returns cart.
detail.place.obstacles: The open study tables offer little conversation privacy, and booked booths are often in demand near deadlines.

detail.design.form: Low pale-oak shelves preserve sightlines to the courtyard windows.
detail.design.materials: Pale-oak shelving and glazed study booths
detail.design.distinctive: Curved lending desk and student-publications display

nodes.name: School office and reception
nodes.description: The public reception and working administrative office handling attendance, visitors, messages, announcements and student inquiries.
nodes.visualDescription: A wide glass reception panel overlooks the atrium. Behind it sit tidy desks, attendance screens, letter trays and an intercom microphone, with navy appointment cards on the counter.

detail.place.purpose: Administration, attendance, visitor management and staff communication.
detail.place.layout: The reception window faces the atrium on the right side of the main entrance. A staff-only door leads behind the counter to the office and a short administrative passage with distinct doors for the principal, guidance office, health room and staff room.
detail.place.access: Students and visitors speak at the public counter. Staff-only areas, medical supplies and confidential records remain beyond controlled doors, with escorted entry as appropriate.
detail.place.routines: Morning attendance and late slips occupy reception after the first bell. Throughout the day staff handle calls, announcements, forms and requests for guidance or health services.
detail.place.resources: Phones, computers, attendance system, visitor sign-in, school intercom, desk microphone, staff-held keys, filing storage and routine forms.
detail.place.obstacles: Queues form at arrival, lunch and dismissal; confidential conversations cannot happen at the public counter.

detail.design.form: A wide glass reception panel overlooks the atrium.
detail.design.materials: Glass reception panel and working desks
detail.design.distinctive: Attendance screens, intercom microphone and letter trays

nodes.name: Principal's office
nodes.description: The high-school principal’s modest private office, used for meetings with students, teachers and families, including discipline and school-event planning.
nodes.visualDescription: A plain timber desk, visitor chairs and framed student artwork face a window toward the front rain garden. A small framed navy-and-silver Hawks pennant sits on a shelf, not as a dominant decoration.

detail.place.purpose: Private school leadership meetings, disciplinary discussions and parent conferences.
detail.place.layout: The office door opens off the administrative passage behind reception. The desk faces a small seating area; a locked cabinet sits along the interior wall.
detail.place.access: Visits are arranged through reception or by staff invitation. Private files remain secured.
detail.place.routines: Brief staff check-ins occur between lessons; longer meetings are usually scheduled outside class-change periods.
detail.place.resources: Desk, visitor seating, school calendar, computer, secure files and conference speaker.
detail.place.obstacles: Sound carries into the administrative passage if the door is open, and unplanned visits may have to wait.

detail.design.form: A plain timber desk, visitor chairs and framed student artwork face a window toward the front rain garden.
detail.design.materials: Timber desk, visitor chairs and artwork
detail.design.colours: Navy and silver in a small Hawks pennant
detail.design.distinctive: Window toward the rain garden and framed student art

nodes.name: Guidance office
nodes.description: A quiet office for academic counselling, course selection, university or employment planning and private student conversations.
nodes.visualDescription: Two soft chairs and a modest desk stand beside a wall of course guides, application calendars and college brochures; frosted glass provides light without opening the room to the hall.

detail.place.purpose: Student advising, course planning and confidential meetings.
detail.place.layout: A dedicated door opens from the administrative passage behind reception, separate from the health room and principal’s office. A small conversation area faces the desk; records are stored in a lockable cabinet.
detail.place.access: Appointments are made through reception or directly with guidance staff. Conversations and records are private.
detail.place.routines: Students come for course requests, timetable changes and planning meetings; some drop-ins are handled between scheduled appointments.
detail.place.resources: Course guides, application information, computer, seating, paper forms and secure student files.
detail.place.obstacles: Appointments can fill near course-registration deadlines; conversations are interrupted if the door is left open.

detail.design.form: Two soft chairs and a modest desk stand beside a wall of course guides, application calendars and college brochures; frosted glass provides light without opening the room to the hall.
detail.design.materials: Soft seating, desk and frosted glass
detail.design.distinctive: Course guides, application calendars and college brochures

nodes.name: Health room
nodes.description: A small student health room for minor injuries, illness and short rests while an authorized staff member arranges appropriate care.
nodes.visualDescription: Clean white cupboards, a sink, examination cot and folding privacy screen sit under soft daylight from frosted lower windows. A navy-blue curtain can screen the cot from the doorway.

detail.place.purpose: Basic first aid, assessment of minor illness and temporary rest.
detail.place.layout: A separate door opens from the administrative passage behind reception. A small waiting chair sits by the entrance; the cot and sink are farther inside, with locked supplies along the interior wall.
detail.place.access: Students usually report to reception before entering, except in urgent situations. Authorized staff control supplies and any private health records.
detail.place.routines: Students visit for everyday ailments or minor injuries throughout the day; the cot is reset between uses and supplies are checked routinely.
detail.place.resources: First-aid supplies, examination cot, sink, clean water, tissues, disposable gloves and locked storage.
detail.place.obstacles: The room has limited space for several visitors at once, and privacy requires the door to remain closed during assessment.

detail.design.form: Clean white cupboards, a sink, examination cot and folding privacy screen sit under soft daylight from frosted lower windows.
detail.design.materials: Cupboards, examination cot, sink and folding screen
detail.design.distinctive: Cot screened from the doorway

nodes.name: Staff room
nodes.description: A comfortable but functional room for staff breaks, brief planning sessions and informal conversations away from student circulation.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale cabinets, a long light-wood table, soft grey seats and a wall of staff pigeonholes sit beneath windows overlooking the front plaza. A crowded mug shelf is its most personal feature.

detail.place.purpose: Staff breaks, preparation, informal meetings and coordination.
detail.place.layout: A door from the staff-only administrative passage behind reception opens to the kitchenette and shared table; pigeonholes and lockers line the far wall. Students do not use it as a shortcut.
detail.place.access: Staff and specifically invited visitors only. Students wait at reception rather than entering.
detail.place.routines: Coffee and briefings happen before the first bell; staff rotate through at breaks and gather for short after-school meetings.
detail.place.resources: Kitchenette, refrigerator, microwave, kettle, worktable, staff pigeonholes, lockers and shared notices.
detail.place.obstacles: The room becomes crowded during breaks, and conversations are not acoustically private.

detail.design.form: Pale cabinets, a long light-wood table, soft grey seats and a wall of staff pigeonholes sit beneath windows overlooking the front plaza.
detail.design.materials: Cabinets, long wood table and grey chairs
detail.design.distinctive: Staff pigeonholes and crowded mug shelf

nodes.name: Auditorium
nodes.description: A compact theatre and assembly hall used for school plays, band concerts, presentations, debates, awards and community events.
nodes.visualDescription: Retractable tiered seating faces a low black stage framed by navy curtains. Pale acoustic timber panels and adjustable high-window blinds keep the room bright or dark as needed. A small Hawks banner hangs by the side entrance.

detail.place.purpose: Assemblies, performances, guest presentations and evening events.
detail.place.layout: Double doors open off the rear-left activity passage from the atrium. Rows of seats face a raised stage; a side stage door leads directly to a separately mapped backstage area, and a lockable control booth overlooks the seats.
detail.place.access: Audiences enter during supervised gatherings or scheduled public events. Stage controls and backstage are accessible to authorized performers and staff.
detail.place.routines: Assemblies interrupt the usual class schedule, while drama rehearsals, concerts and club events often happen after school.
detail.place.resources: Stage, retractable seating, sound system, projection screen, microphones, lighting controls and side-stage access.
detail.place.obstacles: Sound carries into the rear passage; extended seating limits how equipment can be moved across the room.

detail.design.form: Retractable tiered seating faces a low black stage framed by navy curtains.
detail.design.materials: Retractable tiered seating, stage and acoustic timber panels
detail.design.distinctive: High-window blinds and small Hawks banner

nodes.name: Auditorium backstage
nodes.description: A narrow but useful backstage area for actors, musicians and stage crew, with prop storage and direct access to the auditorium stage.
nodes.visualDescription: Black-painted walls, masking curtains, labelled prop shelves, costume rails, a lighted mirror and a scuffed rolling trunk fill the working area.

detail.place.purpose: Stage preparation, props, costumes, scene changes and rehearsal support.
detail.place.layout: A side-stage door opens directly from the auditorium stage into the backstage work zone. A second controlled door reaches the rear-left activity passage so crew members can enter without crossing the audience.
detail.place.access: Authorized performers, stage crew and supervisors use this area during productions. Lighting storage and technical controls are locked when unattended.
detail.place.routines: Used for setup and costume checks before rehearsals or performances; crew members return props to labelled places afterward.
detail.place.resources: Costume rail, make-up mirror, prop shelves, rolling prop trunk, work lights, tape marks and stage access.
detail.place.obstacles: Narrow passages and stored scenery make movement awkward; noise or light behind the curtain can reach the stage.

detail.design.form: Black-painted walls, masking curtains, labelled prop shelves, costume rails, a lighted mirror and a scuffed rolling trunk fill the working area.
detail.design.materials: Painted walls, masking curtains and rolling storage
detail.design.distinctive: Costume rails, prop shelves and lighted mirror

nodes.name: Music room
nodes.description: A well-used teaching and rehearsal room for band, choir, small ensembles and music clubs.
nodes.visualDescription: Tall windows face the courtyard. Black music stands, a slightly worn upright piano, instrument lockers and pale acoustic wall panels fill the room, with a neat row of student concert posters by the door.

detail.place.purpose: Music instruction, rehearsals, practice and storage of school instruments.
detail.place.layout: The rear-left activity passage from the atrium leads past the auditorium to the music-room door. Chairs and stands occupy the central floor; instrument racks line the inner wall, with two small supervised practice booths at the far end.
detail.place.access: Students enter during lessons, rehearsals or authorized practice. Valuable instruments and some booths are secured when not supervised.
detail.place.routines: Classes rehearse during the day; band and choir meet for extra practice after school, especially before concerts.
detail.place.resources: Piano, sheet music, instruments, stands, chairs, metronomes, acoustic panels and practice booths.
detail.place.obstacles: Playing can be heard in the adjacent passage; instruments and stands need clearing to change between ensembles.

detail.design.form: Tall windows face the courtyard.
detail.design.materials: Acoustic wall panels, stands and instrument lockers
detail.design.distinctive: Upright piano, courtyard windows and student concert posters

nodes.name: Cafeteria
nodes.description: The bright main cafeteria, used for lunch, informal conversation, student-club meetings and occasional school events.
nodes.visualDescription: Floor-to-ceiling windows face the courtyard above rows of movable tables. Navy acoustic baffles hang over the serving line, while a large student-painted mural of the nearby river fills one wall. A modest Hawks athletics poster is pinned beside the lunch menu.

detail.place.purpose: Lunch service, social time and flexible school gatherings.
detail.place.layout: A passage from the atrium’s rear-right side leads in. The serving line and staff-only kitchen hatch run along the west wall, while north-facing doors open to the courtyard. Tables fill the centre; an alcove accommodates vending machines and notice stands. The courtyard can be seen through the north windows; the nearby double doors provide the outdoor access.
detail.place.access: Students use the atrium and courtyard doors during supervised periods. The kitchen is separated behind the serving counter.
detail.place.routines: Students arrive in lunch waves, meet friends and carry trays to tables. Staff clean and reset the space afterward; some clubs use a corner after school.
detail.place.resources: Serving counter, tables, chairs, menu boards, drinking-water station, waste sorting, vending alcove and student poster stands. A student-painted river mural fills one wall, alongside ordinary school notices and Hawks athletics posters.
detail.place.obstacles: Queueing students and trays create pinch points during lunch, while large glass surfaces make the room lively and noisy.

detail.design.form: Floor-to-ceiling windows face the courtyard above rows of movable tables.
detail.design.materials: Movable tables, floor-to-ceiling glazing and acoustic baffles
detail.design.distinctive: Student-painted river mural and menu board

nodes.name: School kitchen

nodes.name: Alder Run Homestead
nodes.description: A working but comfortable rural homestead in road-accessible southcentral Alaska, built around a sage-green timber house, rust-red-roofed outbuildings, a garden, small livestock facilities and wooded footpaths. It supports ordinary domestic life, seasonal work and visits without a predetermined household or story.
nodes.visualDescription: A sage-green timber house with a weathered rust-red standing-seam roof stands in a gravel clearing ringed by spruce and paper birch. The outbuildings repeat the same red metal roofing in smaller, mismatched forms. A hand-painted alder-leaf sign marks the drive, and a wind-bent birch at the woods edge is visible from the kitchen window.

detail.place.purpose: Home life, gardening, small-scale animal care, repairs, food preservation, recreation and hosting guests.
detail.place.layout: A private gravel lane enters from a public road to the west and ends in the main yard. The house occupies the north edge; workshop and woodshed are west, animal barn and paddock east, and a fenced garden with a seasonal high tunnel south. The chicken coop and washing/processing shelter sit near the garden; a guest cabin and woodland path lie beyond the yard to the east. The woodland path branches toward a creek bank with footbridge and toward a low ridge overlook. Only representative interior rooms and outdoor areas are mapped.
detail.place.access: The public road and driveway provide ordinary vehicle access, subject to weather and snow clearance. The house and outbuildings have separate doors; fences and gates are not implied shortcuts. The property has grid electricity, a private well, septic system, wood heat and a safely connected backup generator; it is not cut off from nearby services.
detail.place.routines: Spring brings thaw, repairs and seed starting; summer brings long daylight, gardening and outdoor work; autumn brings harvest and winter preparations; winter brings snow clearing, wood hauling and care of animals and heating systems. Trips to town and guests are possible year-round when conditions permit.
detail.place.resources: Household rooms, garden beds, high tunnel, small livestock facilities, tools, covered wood storage, guest sleeping space, maintained paths, well water, utility power and backup systems.
detail.place.obstacles: Mud, ice, snowfall, short winter daylight and the distance between structures change how easy chores and travel are. Wildlife may pass through unfenced land; animals, tools, heating equipment and the creek all require ordinary care. No specific resident, animal personality, incident or conflict is predefined.

nodes.description: A warm, practical timber home with a working kitchen, shared living space and a few private rooms. It is substantial enough for everyday life but plainly built and maintained.
nodes.visualDescription: Sage-green lap siding, deep window trim, a rust-red pitched metal roof with snow guards, and a broad covered porch. The south-facing windows take in the garden; a wood-stove flue rises above the roofline.

detail.place.purpose: Sleeping, meals, indoor leisure, washing and shelter in all seasons.
detail.place.layout: The primary everyday entrance is through the west mudroom from the yard. The mudroom opens to kitchen-dining; the living room is adjacent, with a short private passage to bedrooms and bathroom. The kitchen also opens south onto the covered porch. Pantry storage is directly off the kitchen. Other ordinary bedrooms may exist without separate map nodes.
detail.place.access: Home residents and invited guests enter by the mudroom or porch. Private sleeping spaces and household storage are not automatically open to every visitor.
detail.place.routines: Meals and household tasks organize the day. Wood heat and backup utilities become important in winter, while open windows and the porch are used more in the warmer months.
detail.place.resources: Grid power, private well water with protected lines, indoor plumbing and septic service, wood stove, household furnishings and everyday supplies.
detail.place.obstacles: Wet boots, muddy gear, snow tracked indoors and occasional household maintenance are routine concerns. A loss of outside power does not automatically mean loss of all systems, but backup use requires action.

detail.design.form: Sage-green lap siding, deep window trim, a rust-red pitched metal roof with snow guards, and a broad covered porch.
detail.design.materials: Timber-sided house with pitched standing-seam roof
detail.design.colours: Sage green siding and rust-red roof
detail.design.distinctive: Deep window trim and snow guards

nodes.name: Mudroom and entry
nodes.description: The hard-working threshold between the outdoor yard and the warmth of the house, where boots, coats and tools are left before entering.
nodes.visualDescription: Rubber floor mats, sturdy coat pegs, a bench with boot trays, wool mittens drying on a rack and a narrow window facing the workshop.

detail.place.purpose: Removing outdoor gear, storing frequently used supplies and coming and going.
detail.place.layout: The outer west door steps into the main yard; the inner door leads east into the kitchen-dining room. A shallow closet and utility cupboard line the entry wall. A narrow west-facing window overlooks the workshop across the yard.
detail.place.access: Normal house entrance for residents and welcomed visitors; the locked utility cupboard is for household maintenance rather than casual rummaging.
detail.place.routines: Boots and coats gather in bad weather. Wood for the stove, groceries, animal-care gear and wet outdoor clothing pass through daily.
detail.place.resources: Boot trays, hooks, bench, drying rack, battery lanterns, property map, household key hooks and basic weather gear.
detail.place.obstacles: Bulky coats and stacked boots can crowd the small room; wet floors become slippery.

detail.design.form: Rubber floor mats, sturdy coat pegs, a bench with boot trays, wool mittens drying on a rack and a narrow window facing the workshop.
detail.design.materials: Rubber mats, coat pegs, bench and boot trays
detail.design.distinctive: Mittens drying on a rack and utilitarian coat storage

nodes.name: Kitchen and dining room
nodes.description: The household centre for meals, coffee, preserving garden produce and informal conversation around a sturdy table.
nodes.visualDescription: Pale wooden cabinets, well-used butcher-block counters, a blue enamel kettle, jars on open shelves and a long table by south windows overlooking the garden.

detail.place.purpose: Cooking, shared meals, food preparation and everyday planning.
detail.place.layout: The mudroom opens from the west. A broad opening leads into the living room; a narrow door leads to the pantry. A glazed south door opens onto the covered porch. South-facing windows overlook the garden, but the porch door is the only direct outside exit from this room.
detail.place.access: Usual communal living space; pantry contents and tools belong to the household, even when the table is open to guests.
detail.place.routines: Breakfast and evening meals bookend daily work. Produce is washed, sorted and preserved here in season; coffee and simple indoor chores fill quiet periods.
detail.place.resources: Stove, sink, refrigerator, kettle, table, shelves, cooking equipment, household notebook and drinking water.
detail.place.obstacles: Cooking crowds the counters; large harvests temporarily consume table space. Food should be stored securely rather than left outdoors.

detail.design.form: Pale wooden cabinets, well-used butcher-block counters, a blue enamel kettle, jars on open shelves and a long table by south windows overlooking the garden.
detail.design.materials: Wood cabinets, butcher-block counters and open shelves
detail.design.distinctive: Blue kettle and preserved jars by the window

nodes.name: Living room
nodes.description: A comfortable shared room for reading, talk, quiet evenings and warming up after outside work.
nodes.visualDescription: A black cast-iron wood stove sits on slate tile beneath a simple mantel. There is a faded patterned rug, a patched sofa, board games on shelves and windows onto birch trunks.

detail.place.purpose: Relaxation, indoor social time and a secondary source of house heat.
detail.place.layout: A wide interior opening connects to the kitchen. A short hallway behind the bookcase leads to the private bedroom area and bathroom.
detail.place.access: Ordinary shared family or guest space. The stove and ash handling are managed by people familiar with the equipment.
detail.place.routines: Evenings often gather around the stove in cold weather; long summer evenings may leave the room quiet while people stay outdoors.
detail.place.resources: Wood stove with hearth tools, seating, shelves, books, radio, board games and lamps.
detail.place.obstacles: The stove and hearth are hot in use, and fuel or ash must be managed safely; heavy winter clothing can dry slowly near the doorway.

detail.design.form: A black cast-iron wood stove sits on slate tile beneath a simple mantel.
detail.design.materials: Cast-iron stove, slate hearth and domestic seating
detail.design.colours: Black stove and faded patterned textiles
detail.design.distinctive: Wood stove under simple mantel

nodes.name: Spare bedroom
nodes.description: A simple, unassigned bedroom that can accommodate a household member or overnight guest without establishing a fixed cast.
nodes.visualDescription: A narrow wooden bed, quilt, small dresser, reading lamp and a window facing the stand of birches north of the house.

detail.place.purpose: Sleeping, privacy and storage of personal belongings.
detail.place.layout: A door opens from the short private hall beyond the living room. The bathroom opens separately onto that same hall; this room has no exterior door.
detail.place.access: Normally private even when temporarily unoccupied. Contents may be rearranged to suit whoever uses the room.
detail.place.routines: Used for sleep, changing clothes and retreating from shared rooms; bedding and luggage vary with visitors.
detail.place.resources: Bed, drawers, reading light, blankets, curtains and spare linens.
detail.place.obstacles: Limited floor space and a single entrance make the room poorly suited to storing bulky equipment.

detail.design.form: A narrow wooden bed, quilt, small dresser, reading lamp and a window facing the stand of birches north of the house.

nodes.name: House bathroom
nodes.description: The main indoor washroom serving the mapped household spaces, with normal plumbing rather than an obligatory outdoor privy.
nodes.visualDescription: Plain white tile, a compact bathtub with shower curtain, mirrored cabinet and small frosted window.

detail.place.purpose: Washing, toileting and basic first aid.
detail.place.layout: Reached by a separate door from the private hall beyond the living room, near the spare bedroom. Laundry appliances are tucked into a closet off the hall rather than given a separate node.
detail.place.access: Private while occupied; ordinary household access for residents and invited overnight guests.
detail.place.routines: Used throughout the day; towels and laundry are maintained as part of normal chores.
detail.place.resources: Sink, toilet, bath-shower, mirror, towels, first-aid basics and linen cupboard.
detail.place.obstacles: Only one mapped bathroom serves the house, and winter freeze protection depends on normal heating and insulated plumbing.

detail.design.form: Plain white tile, a compact bathtub with shower curtain, mirrored cabinet and small frosted window.

nodes.name: Pantry and preserves shelves
nodes.description: A cool interior storage room for staples, jars, bulk supplies and shelf-stable food prepared in season.
nodes.visualDescription: Wooden shelves hold labelled jars of jam and pickles, flour tins, dry beans and a calendar of canning dates. A small chest freezer sits against the insulated back wall.

detail.place.purpose: Storing everyday food, preserved produce and household supplies.
detail.place.layout: A single narrow doorway opens directly from the kitchen; shelves run along three walls, leaving a walkway to the freezer.
detail.place.access: Household storage, ordinarily used by residents or with their permission.
detail.place.routines: Stock is checked and rotated. Jars are added after harvest and supplies are replenished during town trips.
detail.place.resources: Dry goods, jars, labels, freezer, food-safe containers, shelving and a small step stool.
detail.place.obstacles: Narrow aisles limit large movements; freezer contents depend on electricity or appropriate backup power.

detail.design.form: Wooden shelves hold labelled jars of jam and pickles, flour tins, dry beans and a calendar of canning dates.
detail.design.distinctive: A small chest freezer sits against the insulated back wall.

nodes.name: Covered south porch
nodes.description: A sheltered outdoor extension of the house, positioned to watch the yard and garden in changing light.
nodes.visualDescription: Unpainted boards and weathered green rocking chairs sit beneath a deep roof. A small brass bell hangs near the kitchen door, and boots collect beside a boot scraper.

detail.place.purpose: Sitting outdoors, watching weather, conversation and a second house entry.
detail.place.layout: The porch extends along the south face of the house. A glazed door connects directly to the kitchen; a short set of steps descends to the yard-side garden path.
detail.place.access: Household and invited visitor use. The porch steps remain an exterior route, not an entrance to the woodland without passing the yard or garden path.
detail.place.routines: In summer it serves as a place for tea and breaks; in winter snow is brushed from the steps and stored wood may be brought near the door for immediate use.
detail.place.resources: Rocking chairs, small table, brass bell, boot scraper and views of the garden and yard.
detail.place.obstacles: Ice on steps and roof-shed snow require attention; outdoor seating may be unusable in severe weather.

detail.design.form: Unpainted boards and weathered green rocking chairs sit beneath a deep roof.
detail.design.distinctive: A small brass bell hangs near the kitchen door, and boots collect beside a boot scraper.

nodes.name: Workshop and garage
nodes.description: A combined one-bay garage and woodworking/repair shop for tools, vehicle maintenance and seasonal projects.
nodes.visualDescription: A barn-red sliding garage door fronts weathered timber siding. Inside are pegboard tools, a scarred workbench, hanging extension cords and a concrete floor swept around old stains.

detail.place.purpose: Building, repairing, maintaining vehicles and preparing equipment for each season.
detail.place.layout: Large doors open east onto the gravel yard; a person-door is on the south side. A covered equipment shelter attaches outside along the south wall, and the woodshed stands a few steps northwest.
detail.place.access: The shop is normally locked when unused. Powered equipment, vehicles and sharp tools are operated only by capable and authorised users.
detail.place.routines: Summer repairs and winter preparations keep the bench busy. Tools are returned to marked storage and the floor is cleared for vehicle work.
detail.place.resources: Workbench, vise, shelves, hand and power tools, jack, work lights, spare parts and small hardware bins.
detail.place.obstacles: Vehicle projects take up the single bay. Noisy tools, sharp edges, flammables and stored equipment make casual exploration risky.

detail.design.form: A barn-red sliding garage door fronts weathered timber siding.
detail.design.distinctive: Inside are pegboard tools, a scarred workbench, hanging extension cords and a concrete floor swept around old stains.

nodes.name: Equipment lean-to
nodes.description: A roofed, open-sided parking bay beside the shop for the homestead's small utility equipment and winter gear.
nodes.visualDescription: Corrugated roofing covers a utility ATV, tow sled, snow shovel rack and stacked tires. Packed earth is striped with muddy tracks.

detail.place.purpose: Keeping portable equipment close to the yard without occupying the repair shop.
detail.place.layout: Attached to the workshop's south exterior wall and open to a gravel spur circling from the main yard; a path continues northwest to the woodshed. There is no interior door into the workshop.
detail.place.access: Accessible from the yard to the household and approved helpers. Engines and any backup generator run only in a safe, well-ventilated outdoor position away from openings.
detail.place.routines: The ATV may haul feed and supplies on suitable ground; winter gear is checked and snow-clearing implements are moved here between storms.
detail.place.resources: Utility ATV, tow sled, shovels, spare tires, cargo straps and a secured outdoor-rated generator connection point.
detail.place.obstacles: Sheltered equipment can still ice over; engines and exhaust are hazards, and the bay is cramped when everything is parked.

detail.design.form: Corrugated roofing covers a utility ATV, tow sled, snow shovel rack and stacked tires.
detail.design.distinctive: Packed earth is striped with muddy tracks.

nodes.name: Woodshed and chopping block
nodes.description: A simple roofed storage area holding split firewood, kindling and tools needed for heating the house.
nodes.visualDescription: Neat rows of birch and spruce firewood rest on raised rails under a broad tin roof. A chopping block stands outside, its surface silvered with axe marks.

detail.place.purpose: Drying, storing and splitting household firewood.
detail.place.layout: Just northwest of the main house, between the workshop-side path and the yard, allowing wood to be taken to the mudroom without crossing animal pens.
detail.place.access: Household work area. Cutting tools are stored securely, and children or visitors should not treat it as a play space.
detail.place.routines: Wood is stacked through the warmer months and carried in small loads during cold weather.
detail.place.resources: Stacked firewood, kindling box, chopping block, splitting maul and handcart.
detail.place.obstacles: Splinters, swinging tools, uneven frozen ground and falling stacked logs require care.

detail.design.form: Neat rows of birch and spruce firewood rest on raised rails under a broad tin roof.
detail.design.distinctive: A chopping block stands outside, its surface silvered with axe marks.

nodes.name: Fenced kitchen garden
nodes.description: A productive but modest set of vegetable beds that changes dramatically between the long summer growing season and winter snow.
nodes.visualDescription: Raised timber beds form an orderly patchwork behind wire fencing. A bright yellow gate latch and a hand-painted crop marker make the garden recognisable even when beds are bare.

detail.place.purpose: Growing vegetables and herbs for household use.
detail.place.layout: South of the house across a short path from the porch and yard. A gate faces north toward the yard; the high tunnel occupies the garden's sunnier eastern edge. The berry patch lies outside the west fence.
detail.place.access: Gate closes to discourage browsing wildlife and loose animals. Household gardeners and supervised visitors may enter by the gate.
detail.place.routines: Beds are planted after thaw, watered and weeded in the growing season, harvested in late summer and autumn, and covered or left dormant in winter.
detail.place.resources: Raised beds, soil, watering hoses, compost bins with appropriate wildlife protection, hand tools, plant labels and a gate.
detail.place.obstacles: Moose or smaller wildlife can damage crops if the gate is left open; season length, frost, wet ground and pests limit growth.

detail.design.form: Raised timber beds form an orderly patchwork behind wire fencing.
detail.design.distinctive: A bright yellow gate latch and a hand-painted crop marker make the garden recognisable even when beds are bare.

nodes.name: Seasonal high tunnel
nodes.description: An unheated, walk-in growing tunnel that extends the useful gardening season rather than producing tropical crops year-round.
nodes.visualDescription: Translucent plastic stretched over curved metal ribs holds long rows of greens and tomatoes in season. Rolled side vents and a repaired patch on one end panel show regular use.

detail.place.purpose: Protecting seedlings and crops from chilly weather and extending the local growing season.
detail.place.layout: Stands just inside the eastern garden fence. Its north door opens onto the main garden path between raised beds; rows and a narrow centre walkway run south from the door.
detail.place.access: Reached through the fenced garden. Doors and vents are secured outside active use, and the structure is not a heated winter living space.
detail.place.routines: Seedlings and soil preparation begin as the season allows; ventilation and watering are daily warm-season tasks. The covering and supports are secured or maintained for winter loads.
detail.place.resources: In-ground beds, hose, thermometer, watering can, seed trays, trellis string and roll-up vents.
detail.place.obstacles: Bright sun can overheat the interior even on cool days; frost, wind and snow can damage the structure if unmanaged.

detail.design.form: Translucent plastic stretched over curved metal ribs holds long rows of greens and tomatoes in season.
detail.design.distinctive: Rolled side vents and a repaired patch on one end panel show regular use.

nodes.name: Berry patch and rhubarb bed
nodes.description: A small, established patch of currants, raspberries and rhubarb along the cultivated edge of the clearing.
nodes.visualDescription: Uneven berry canes grow beside a low split-rail border; broad rhubarb leaves spill toward a flat stone used as a picking stool.

detail.place.purpose: Picking seasonal fruit, tending perennials and casual outdoor breaks.
detail.place.layout: Outside the west fence of the kitchen garden, accessible along the same path from the yard. It does not provide a passage through the fenced vegetable beds.
detail.place.access: Normally open to the household and visitors with permission; fruit is not assumed available outside its season.
detail.place.routines: Canes are pruned and mulched, fruit is picked when ripe, and leaves and beds go dormant in colder months.
detail.place.resources: Berry bushes, rhubarb, mulch, hand snips, baskets and a small sitting stone.
detail.place.obstacles: Thorns, mosquitoes, damp soil and wildlife attracted by ripe fruit can complicate harvesting.

detail.design.form: Uneven berry canes grow beside a low split-rail border; broad rhubarb leaves spill toward a flat stone used as a picking stool.

nodes.name: Chicken coop and enclosed run
nodes.description: A compact poultry house with a fenced exercise run for a small flock, close enough for daily care but away from the kitchen door.
nodes.visualDescription: The little red coop has a silver metal roof, nest-box access flap and a fenced run with wire mesh overhead. A chalkboard by the latch lists ordinary feeding notes.

detail.place.purpose: Housing poultry and collecting eggs for household use.
detail.place.layout: Southeast of the garden, reached along a gravel footpath from the yard. A latched gate opens to the enclosed run; a smaller door leads into the coop. Neither connects to the goat paddock.
detail.place.access: The run is latched and the coop secured against predators. Visitors should not enter or feed animals without the caretaker's agreement.
detail.place.routines: Feeding, watering, bedding care and egg collection recur daily. Cold and shorter daylight affect the routine and egg production.
detail.place.resources: Nest boxes, roosts, feed and water equipment, bedding, latches and egg basket.
detail.place.obstacles: Slippery ground, predator pressure and the need for daily water and feeding limit how long animals can be left unattended.

detail.design.form: The little red coop has a silver metal roof, nest-box access flap and a fenced run with wire mesh overhead.
detail.design.distinctive: A chalkboard by the latch lists ordinary feeding notes.

nodes.name: Small animal barn
nodes.description: A simple, well-maintained timber barn for a few small livestock animals, feed storage and grooming rather than a commercial stable.
nodes.visualDescription: Faded red doors open onto a central aisle, with two low stalls, hanging halters, hay bales on a raised rack and winter light through a narrow window.

detail.place.purpose: Sheltering and tending a few goats or similarly sized domestic animals.
detail.place.layout: On the east edge of the main yard. Double doors face west into the yard; an east stock gate opens directly into the adjacent fenced paddock. A feed corner occupies the north wall.
detail.place.access: Stock gates stay latched. Animals are handled by people who know them; feed storage is secured from wildlife and pests.
detail.place.routines: Feeding, watering, bedding changes and checks happen every day, with extra attention during severe winter weather.
detail.place.resources: Stalls, hay rack, feed bin, grooming brushes, buckets, water supply and basic animal-handling equipment.
detail.place.obstacles: Animals can block passages; hay dust, manure, icy thresholds and secure latches require routine attention.

detail.design.form: Faded red doors open onto a central aisle, with two low stalls, hanging halters, hay bales on a raised rack and winter light through a narrow window.

nodes.name: Fenced paddock
nodes.description: A modest outdoor enclosure where small livestock can graze, browse and spend time outside their shelter.
nodes.visualDescription: Wire-and-post fencing surrounds rough grass, a scuffed wooden gate and a sheltered water trough. Spruce trees stand beyond the east fence.

detail.place.purpose: Safe outdoor space and exercise for the small livestock kept at the barn.
detail.place.layout: Directly east of the barn, connected through its stock gate; a second latched pedestrian gate opens to the eastern yard path for caretakers. It is not a through-route into the woods.
detail.place.access: Gates remain closed during normal use. Entry among animals is supervised by their caretaker.
detail.place.routines: Water is checked, ground is cleaned as needed and fencing inspected, especially after storms and winter thaw.
detail.place.resources: Fenced turnout, trough, hay feeder, shelter edge and gate latches.
detail.place.obstacles: Icy or muddy ground, damaged fencing and curious animals can make handling difficult.

detail.design.form: Wire-and-post fencing surrounds rough grass, a scuffed wooden gate and a sheltered water trough.
detail.design.distinctive: Spruce trees stand beyond the east fence.

nodes.name: Covered wash and processing shelter
nodes.description: An outdoor work area for washing vegetables, cleaning fish obtained elsewhere and preparing harvests before they enter the home.
nodes.visualDescription: A galvanized worktop stands beneath a simple roof, with a wash basin, outdoor tap, hoses on hooks, a large draining board and a lidded, wildlife-resistant waste container.

detail.place.purpose: Messy seasonal food-preparation jobs kept separate from the household kitchen.
detail.place.layout: Southwest of the yard behind the workshop, with an open side facing the path to the garden. The return path to the kitchen crosses the yard; it does not open into the workshop.
detail.place.access: Work surface is available to household members. Food preparation follows normal hygiene and waste-storage practices; the shelter is not used for indoor overnight storage.
detail.place.routines: Busy during harvest and occasional fish-processing days, but quiet much of the year. Equipment is cleaned, drained and winterised as conditions require.
detail.place.resources: Wash basin, hose, sturdy worktable, cleaning tools, drying racks and secure waste storage.
detail.place.obstacles: Outdoor water lines must be drained or protected before freezing; wildlife and insects make exposed food and scraps a concern.

detail.design.form: A galvanized worktop stands beneath a simple roof, with a wash basin, outdoor tap, hoses on hooks, a large draining board and a lidded, wildlife-resistant waste container.
detail.design.materials: Galvanized work surface and simple overhead shelter
detail.design.distinctive: Outdoor tap, hoses and wash basin

nodes.name: Yard fire circle
nodes.description: A small open-air gathering place for evenings, stories and warming up after outdoor work.
nodes.visualDescription: A ring of fieldstones surrounds a shallow ash bed, with rough log benches and a battered metal kettle hook. The trees are set back from the cleared gravel around it.

detail.place.purpose: Outdoor conversation, simple cooking and recreation when conditions allow.
detail.place.layout: On the southeastern edge of the main yard, between the garden path and the start of the eastern footpath. The clearing is separate from buildings, stacked wood and animal fences.
detail.place.access: Available when local fire restrictions and weather permit. Fires require competent attendance and full extinguishing.
detail.place.routines: Used for occasional evening gatherings, particularly in milder weather; snow may cover the benches for much of winter.
detail.place.resources: Stone fire ring, benches, a covered bucket of water or appropriate extinguisher and a small cooking grate.
detail.place.obstacles: Smoke, sparks, wind, mosquitoes and changing fire restrictions can limit use.

detail.design.form: A ring of fieldstones surrounds a shallow ash bed, with rough log benches and a battered metal kettle hook.
detail.design.materials: Fieldstone fire ring and rough log seating
detail.design.distinctive: Metal ash bucket beside the ring

nodes.name: Little guest cabin
nodes.description: A separate one-room cabin for visiting family, friends or temporary helpers, offering privacy without inventing any permanent occupant.
nodes.visualDescription: A squat cedar cabin under the same rust-red roof style has a small porch, two glowing windowpanes and an old enamel number 2 fixed beside the door.

detail.place.purpose: Temporary sleeping space, quiet work and retreat from the busy main house.
detail.place.layout: Reached by a short, signposted path east of the main yard, before the woodland trail fork. Inside, the door opens to one room with sleeping bunks, a small sitting table and storage; a compact enclosed stove stands against the far wall. The cabin has no separate road or direct barn entrance.
detail.place.access: Normally locked when empty, but may be made available to invited guests. It has electric light and a heater; guests use the bathroom in the main house rather than an invented private bath.
detail.place.routines: Prepared and aired before visits; in cold months it must be heated before use and the short path cleared.
detail.place.resources: Two bunks, bedding, small table, shelves, electric lamps, safe room heat and a porch bench.
detail.place.obstacles: Cold interiors after disuse, icy path sections and the lack of indoor plumbing make it less convenient than the house.

detail.design.form: A squat cedar cabin under the same rust-red roof style has a small porch, two glowing windowpanes and an old enamel number 2 fixed beside the door.
detail.design.materials: Cedar cabin and rust-red roof
detail.design.distinctive: Small porch and two windows

nodes.name: Spruce-and-birch footpath
nodes.description: A lightly maintained walking path through the woods immediately beyond the working yard, useful for short walks and small chores.
nodes.visualDescription: A narrow earth track winds between black spruce and paper birch. Three simple wooden direction markers have painted alder leaves, and the undergrowth opens in patches of moss.

detail.place.purpose: Walking, exploring the property and reaching the creek and overlook.
detail.place.layout: Begins east of the yard near the wind-bent birch and passes the guest cabin. At a marked fork, the south path reaches the creek bank; the north path rises gently to the ridge overlook. Neither branch is a vehicle road.
detail.place.access: Ordinary foot access is possible for the household and approved guests. The path stays on the homestead; its markers do not imply access to other people's land.
detail.place.routines: Used for walks, checking fallen branches and visiting the creek. Conditions shift with thaw, vegetation, snow depth and animal activity.
detail.place.resources: Foot-worn trail, simple waymarkers, short corduroy planks over one damp spot and views of common boreal woodland. Three wooden direction markers painted with alder leaves distinguish the trail branches.
detail.place.obstacles: Roots, mosquitoes, slick logs, deep snow and limited winter daylight make travel slower. Wild animals should be given space.

detail.design.form: A narrow earth track winds between black spruce and paper birch.
detail.design.materials: Narrow earth track with spruce, birch and moss
detail.design.colours: Dark spruce and pale birch bark
detail.design.distinctive: Three alder-leaf direction markers

nodes.name: Creek bank
nodes.description: A narrow stream along the lower part of the property, bordered by willows and mossy banks, visited more for quiet than for utility.
nodes.visualDescription: Cold brown-green water slips over gravel beneath overhanging willows. An old alder leans downstream beside a weathered timber footbridge.

detail.place.purpose: Quiet walks, watching the water and an outdoor landmark.
detail.place.layout: The south branch of the woodland path reaches a small gravel bank above the creek. A wooden footbridge spans this same crossing, leading to the far bank; it is the only maintained crossing in the mapped property.
detail.place.access: Open to foot visitors in safe conditions, not a drinking-water supply or a guaranteed safe route across ice.
detail.place.routines: Water level changes with rain and melt; the bank is more often visited in summer than in icy periods.
detail.place.resources: Gravel bank, creek views, driftwood and access to the timber footbridge.
detail.place.obstacles: Cold water, muddy footing, spring runoff and unstable ice make entering or crossing the stream hazardous. The sound of moving water can obscure quiet speech close to the bank, especially during spring runoff.

detail.design.form: Cold brown-green water slips over gravel beneath overhanging willows.
detail.design.materials: Gravel streambed and willow-lined bank
detail.design.distinctive: Alder tree and visible timber footbridge

nodes.name: Timber footbridge
nodes.description: A short pedestrian bridge that makes the creek crossing feel like a genuine part of the property.
nodes.visualDescription: Silvered wooden planks and low timber rails span the water; one rail bears a simple hand-carved alder-leaf motif.

detail.place.purpose: Crossing the creek on foot and pausing to watch the water below.
detail.place.layout: The near end joins the creek bank reached from the southern woodland path; the far end reaches a short patch of woods on the opposite bank. No named interior or road is reached directly from the bridge.
detail.place.access: Foot traffic only. The bridge is checked and may be avoided when damaged or covered in deep snow.
detail.place.routines: Mostly used in mild weather; rails and boards are checked after thaw and high water.
detail.place.resources: Planked deck, handrails and a view upstream and downstream.
detail.place.obstacles: Frost, wet boards, high water and seasonal wear reduce traction and safety.

detail.design.form: Silvered wooden planks and low timber rails span the water; one rail bears a simple hand-carved alder-leaf motif.
detail.design.materials: Timber planks and low wooden rails
detail.design.distinctive: Carved alder-leaf mark on a rail

nodes.name: Low ridge overlook
nodes.description: A quiet spot on a modest rise, high enough to see the homestead clearing and distant hills on a clear day.
nodes.visualDescription: The trees part around a broad, lichen-speckled rock and an unpainted plank bench. A bend in the treeline frames the red roofs below; distant mountains appear only in clear weather.

detail.place.purpose: Walking destination, reflection and looking out over the property.
detail.place.layout: Reached from the north fork of the woodland path by a short uphill trail. The route ends here and returns to the same path; it does not connect to the public road.
detail.place.access: Normal walking access when weather and footing allow. No railings, lights or vehicle approach are provided.
detail.place.routines: Used for brief stops, quiet talks and occasional views of weather moving across the valley.
detail.place.resources: Bench, exposed rock, tree-framed panorama and an unobstructed view back toward the homestead.
detail.place.obstacles: Wind exposure, snow, slippery rock and poor visibility can make the site uncomfortable or unsafe.

detail.place.purpose: Secure transport and handling of supplies, equipment and survey specimens.
detail.place.layout: The cargo bay opens from the aft engineering passage through a pressure door. Its central aisle reaches the inner aft airlock; an interior hatch off one side opens into the sample-analysis room, while a separately sealed service hatch connects to the shuttle berth when docked.
detail.place.access: Crew enter through engineering or the inner airlock. Shuttle access is available only with a secured and equalized docking connection; the service hatch does not open freely to space.
detail.place.routines: Cargo is inventoried and tied down before maneuvers; incoming survey samples may be transferred to analysis once properly handled.
detail.place.resources: Tie-down rails, loading equipment, sample-transfer counter, pressure doors and open stowage bays.
detail.place.obstacles: Stowed loads and handling gear constrain the clear aisle; hatches and pressure boundaries must remain unobstructed.

detail.place.purpose: Receive, catalogue and examine ordinary survey samples before long-term storage or transport.
detail.place.layout: A sealed interior hatch off the cargo bay opens into a small laboratory with a central examination bench, instrument rack and secure specimen shelves. There is no independent exterior exit.
detail.place.access: Reached from the cargo bay after samples are transferred under suitable handling procedures; hazardous materials require separate precautions as established by a story.
detail.place.routines: Samples can be logged, labeled and examined as missions require; the starter establishes neither collected specimens nor experimental results.
detail.place.resources: Sealable specimen containers, magnifier, imaging station, cataloguing console and clean work surface.
detail.place.obstacles: The room has little free bench area, and uncontained specimens may require isolation before examination.

detail.place.purpose: Boarding, docking and controlled suited access to the exterior.
detail.place.layout: The inner pressure hatch opens from the cargo-bay aisle; an outer hatch opens to a compatible dock or the exterior, with pressure controls between them.
detail.place.access: Only one hatch is normally opened at a time, after appropriate pressure equalization; external access needs an established safe environment or appropriate protective equipment.
detail.place.routines: Hatch seals, pressure readings and suit provisions are checked when preparing for a transfer or external work.
detail.place.resources: Pressure controls, gauge, handholds, tether points and a recessed suit locker.
detail.place.obstacles: Door interlocks and pressure changes restrict passage; opening the exterior hatch is not a normal corridor shortcut.

detail.place.purpose: Docking, limited exterior servicing and transfer between a small compatible shuttle and the ship.
detail.place.layout: The aft external berth includes alignment guides, docking clamps and a service platform. Its connection to the cargo bay passes through a sealable service hatch and becomes a boarding passage only when a shuttle is secured and the connection is pressure-tight.
detail.place.access: The berth is not a pressurized room when empty; entry from cargo requires a verified docking seal or appropriate exterior-access procedures. No shuttle is present by default.
detail.place.routines: Connections and clamps are checked during arrival, departure and planned servicing; the berth remains unused when no craft is docked.
detail.place.resources: Docking clamps, service umbilicals, alignment marks and a maintenance platform.
detail.place.obstacles: An undocked berth is exposed to space; a hatch alone does not provide a safe route outside.

nodes.name: Wayfarer narration style
nodes.description: Editable default prose style for a small-crew science-fiction setting, without inventing a crew or mission.

core.narration-style.instructions: Use precise, readable science-fiction prose attentive to the physical ship layout, watch routines and limits of equipment. Technical details should remain comprehensible and consistent; do not invent a crisis, mission outcome, alien contact or crew history.

detail.visual-style.palette: White and slate hull finishes, warm neutral habitation spaces, dark service panels and amber work lights.
detail.visual-style.lighting: Practical shipboard light sources and plausible viewport illumination; preserve darkness or conditions established by the scene.
detail.visual-style.composition: Human-scale ship interiors with clear corridors, doors and operational areas; exterior views show physically plausible scale.
detail.visual-style.instructions: Preserve the vessel’s established compartments, pressure boundaries and component designs. Do not add crew, shuttles, specimens or space phenomena without story support.

nodes.name: Wayfarer story direction

detail.brief.premise: A compact, functional three-deck survey vessel able to support small crews on extended expeditions, with labs, engineering, habitation and cargo access.
detail.brief.genre: Open-ended science fiction; suitable for exploration, crew life, mystery or technical problem-solving.
detail.brief.themes: Cooperation, curiosity, routine, discovery and the practical cost of operating far from support can emerge if established.
detail.brief.aims: Leave the crew, destination, mission, events, discoveries and conflicts for the author and later story development.

nodes.name: Wayfarer vessel background

detail.lore.content: The Wayfarer is a small survey ship with a command deck, habitation deck, engineering deck, cargo bay, specimen laboratory, aft airlock and external shuttle berth. A central lift and ladderwell connect main decks; its pressurized compartments are separated by doors and hatches. Exterior access requires appropriate docking or protective procedures.
detail.lore.significance: Keeps the ship’s layout and operational limits consistent without committing to any particular planet, crew, discovery or voyage.

nodes.name: Pressure and exterior access

detail.rule.rule: A sealed pressure boundary must be checked and equalized before transfer. Viewports and unsecured service hatches do not provide direct habitable access to space; a shuttle berth is not pressurized unless a compatible craft is correctly docked.
detail.rule.scope: Wayfarer pressure compartments, airlock, cargo connections and shuttle berth.
detail.rule.exceptions: Alternative technologies or procedures require explicit establishment in a particular story; no shortcut is assumed by default.
